resources.string: Know your risk: find evacuation routes and high-ground shelters near you.
Pack a go-bag: flashlight, spare batteries, first-aid kit, medicines, drinking water, dry food and a power bank.
Keep IDs, insurance cards, emergency contacts and important documents in a waterproof bag.
Keep phones and power banks charged, and store emergency food and clean drinking water.
Move valuables, electronics, vehicles and pets to higher ground before water rises.
Learn how to switch off electricity and gas safely — only ever do it when it is safe to do so.
Arrange early evacuation help for children, elderly people, pregnant women and people with disabilities.
Keep a battery or hand-crank radio and learn your local warning signals.
Agree one family meeting point and one out-of-area contact everyone can reach.
Save FloodCue\'s emergency numbers, and test the siren and SOS screens once before the monsoon.
Keep the vehicle fuelled during flood season — you may need to leave at short notice.
Move to higher ground immediately — do not wait to see how high the water will rise.
Never walk, swim or drive through floodwater. Avoid flooded roads, bridges and underpasses.
Avoid touching electrical equipment, sockets or power lines that are near water.
Moving water is stronger than it looks: 15 cm can knock you off your feet and about 60 cm can float a car.
Keep children away from floodwater and fast-flowing drains.
Follow official evacuation instructions and avoid contact with contaminated floodwater.
Drink only safe water and avoid food contaminated by floodwater.
If trapped, move to a safe elevated place and contact emergency services when possible.
Signal for rescue: wave a bright cloth by day; at night flash a flashlight in repeated SOS patterns or use a phone torch.
Use a whistle, mirror or other visible signal to attract rescuers — they spot these before they spot you.
No phone signal? Keep retrying emergency calls when possible and signal nearby rescuers without putting yourself at risk.
Do not light fires or create smoke indoors or near flammable materials. Use smoke signals only when it is safe and cannot start a fire.
Turn off electricity and gas at the main before water reaches sockets, only if it is safe to do so.
Keep your phone dry and save its battery — you may need it to call for help.
Go to the highest floor; move onto the roof only as a last resort.
Listen to official alerts on a radio if the power and internet are out.
Return home only when authorities declare it safe.
Stay away from damaged buildings, fallen power lines and electrical equipment exposed to water.
Do not switch on any electrical appliance until it has been inspected and declared safe.
Discard food contaminated by floodwater and drink only safe, treated water.
Wear protective footwear and gloves while cleaning up.
Photograph property damage for insurance if it is safe, and seek medical help for injuries or contaminated-water exposure.
Wash your hands and any cuts thoroughly after contact with floodwater.
Dry and ventilate buildings quickly to stop mould from growing.
Boil or treat drinking water until the supply is declared safe.
Watch for snakes, insects or animals brought in by the floodwater.
